clue.text: Game bird possibly returning, for example

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of bird may be arranged some other way
returning tells us to read the abbreviation backwards

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a game bird, perhaps a returning one, as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' opens the clue like an adjective for the bird, but it is the definition; 'possibly' and 'returning' work on the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a well-known card game played by two partnerships.

clue.text: Ordered fabulous bird to appear in expensive cloth

indicators.note: to appear in tells us one piece shows up within the other

parts.note: bade is a past tense of bid, meaning ordered
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A command is given for a mythical bird to be shown on costly fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Brocade is a rich woven fabric with raised patterns, often of silk and gold thread.

clue.text: Playwright fails to open in Bury

indicators.note: fails to open means the first letter of the word is missing

parts.note: Harold Pinter was a British dramatist

explanation.surface: A dramatist's play flops on its first night in the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town, but it is the verb, to bury.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter a body is to bury it in a grave.

clue.text: He takes a risk getting note on author

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: G is a musical note
Eric Ambler was an English thriller writer

explanation.surface: A risk-taker gets a musical note put on top of a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler is someone who bets money, a person who takes chances.

clue.text: Teach child painting

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: Teach a youngster how to paint.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart knowledge is to pass it on, as a teacher does.

clue.text: He who switches hat with mama is a wise man!

indicators.note: switches says the letters are moved around into new places

explanation.surface: Anyone who swaps a hat with their mother must be a sage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switches' rearranges HAT and MAMA together; 'He who' and 'is' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma is an Indian title of respect for a holy or wise person, as given to Gandhi.

clue.text: Mark fooled about, but was given the job

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: aped means mimicked or made fun of, hence fooled
a point is a mark, as in a dot

explanation.surface: Mark played the fool, yet still landed the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the word for fooled around the mark; 'but' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person appointed to a post has been chosen for it, so was given the job.

clue.text: They work at sea and on the land

definitions.meaning: people or machines that cultivate soil

explanation.definitionFit: A tiller steers a boat, and a tiller is also one who tills a field.

clue.text: Able to pay for a powerful car

parts.note: F stands for forte, loud or strong in music
Ford is a car maker

explanation.surface: Able to buy a high-performance motor.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford something is to have enough money to be able to buy it.

clue.text: Parrot's tail getting the fewest votes?

definitions.meaning: Poll is a traditional pet name for a parrot, so its tail is its rear end
last place in an election count

explanation.definitionFit: A pet parrot is called Poll, and coming last in a ballot is being lowest in the poll.

clue.text: Watch what goes round

definitions.meaning: to keep watch over an area
a guard or unit doing the rounds

explanation.definitionFit: A patrol keeps watch, and it goes round an area on a regular beat.

clue.text: He is not given much hope of changing our diets

definitions.text: He is not given much hope

indicators.note: changing says these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is unlikely to succeed in altering our eating habits.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider is a competitor thought to have little chance of winning.

clue.text: Alluded to as arbitrator who went wrong

parts.note: ref is short for referee, an arbitrator
erred means made a mistake

explanation.surface: A match official who made a blunder was mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is referred to, it is mentioned or alluded to.

clue.text: Where people go in for charms

definitions.meaning: delights or enchants, stressed on the second syllable

explanation.definitionFit: Entrances are doorways, and to entrance someone is to charm them.

clue.text: Attending trial to give evidence

parts.note: at means present at, attending
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A witness attends a court trial to give testimony.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or declare something true.

clue.text: Got on one's nerves when scratched

definitions.meaning: rubbed harshly, as a grater shreds

explanation.definitionFit: Grated means irritated, and also scraped against a rough surface.

clue.text: Curl round impediment

parts.note: a ring is round in shape
let is an old word for a hindrance, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A lock of hair gets twisted round some obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a long spiral curl of hair.

clue.text: Run and start to dance on water

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: the Ribble is a river in Lancashire, England

explanation.surface: Sprint, then begin to dance on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ribble is a river in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To dribble is to run or trickle in a small stream.

clue.text: Rose, perhaps, to the required level

definitions.meaning: a plant trained on an upright stem, such as a rose

explanation.definitionFit: A standard rose grows on a tall single stem, and a standard is an accepted level of quality.

clue.text: Holds a tiresome group to ridicule

indicators.note: group signals a run of letters taken across the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a boring crowd up for mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Holds' through 'a' and into 'tiresome'.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire uses ridicule and irony to mock folly or vice.

clue.text: Mad liar working to become an officer

indicators.note: working says these letters are being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A crazy fibber gets on and rises to high rank.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a senior naval officer.

clue.text: Soldier tried swimming and gave up

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: swimming says the letters move around freely

explanation.surface: A soldier attempted to swim, then quit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who retired stopped working, giving up their career.

clue.text: Girl with catalogue is interested in records

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A girl with an inventory takes an interest in archives.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist writes historical chronicles, so is a person interested in records.

clue.text: I'm backing the teachers to get the point in time

indicators.note: backing means the letters are read from the back

parts.note: NUT is the National Union of Teachers
E is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone supports teachers to make their point in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns I'm round. 'point' here is a compass point, and only 'time' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute is a short span of time.

clue.text: At no time does revenue start rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read upwards
start means the opening part of the word revenue

explanation.surface: Income never goes up from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' takes REVEN from 'revenue'; 'rising' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Never means on no occasion, at no time at all.

clue.text: Eleven city cars

parts.note: Blackburn is a town in Lancashire, England
Rover was a British car maker

explanation.surface: Eleven cars are seen in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: An eleven is a football team; Blackburn Rovers is a club in English football.
explanation.definitionFit: A football side has eleven players, so a club team is an eleven.

clue.text: Inspector to try English recipe

parts.note: to test is to try
R is short for recipe, used on prescriptions

explanation.surface: An inspector attempts an English recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester is someone who checks or inspects things.

clue.text: By mistake, Gerald scowled

indicators.note: by mistake suggests the letters have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gerald frowned when he got it wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To glare is to stare angrily, much like scowling.
